memos.headline: S09 Stands Alone at 52-Week Highs While Broad Weakness Drags Most Names Below Key Averages
memos.body: I see a deeply bifurcated tape across this universe as of March 13. S09 is the clear standout—sitting at its 52-week high with +32.6% over 12 weeks, +30.3% above its 200-day mean, and relative strength vs SPY of +35.3% over 12 weeks; RSI at 64.4 is elevated but not yet overbought. On the other end, S06 (RSI 32.2, -8.7% rel strength 12w) and S04 (drawdown -27.0%, -18.1% below 200d mean) are in clear downtrends with no sign of stabilization. S05 and S07 retain strong longer-term uptrends (26w returns of +28.6% and +64.0% respectively) but are pulling back sharply toward their 50-day means—I'd wait for RSI to firm before adding. S02's -52.9% drawdown from its 52-week high is a red flag suggesting structural damage, not a dip to buy. I would ride S09's momentum, nibble S05 on a hold of the 200-day area, and avoid the broken charts in S06, S04, and S02.

views.note: At 52-week highs with massive relative strength; would reassess if price breaks below the 50-day mean (~141 implied by +10.5% premium).
Strong 26w trend (+28.6%) and +17.9% above 200d mean cushion the pullback; a close below ~256 (200d area) would flip me neutral.
Massive 26w gain (+64%) but 4w return of -8.5% and high ATR (4.25%) suggest a volatile consolidation; need RSI to reclaim 50 before getting constructive.
Mildly positive 12w and 26w returns with price near the 200d mean; no strong signal either way, watching for a break above the 50d to turn long.
RSI 32.2 is the lowest in the universe, -8.7% relative strength over 12w, and price is -7.8% below the 50d mean—clear downtrend; would reconsider above 305 (50d area).
Down -27% from 52w high and -18.1% below 200d mean; this is a broken chart and I see no reason to step in front of it until price reclaims at least 430.
A -52.9% drawdown from 52w high dwarfs everything else in this universe; even with a slight 4w stabilization, the structural damage is too severe.
RSI 34.6 is approaching oversold but the 12w return of -8.8% and negative relative strength suggest catching a falling knife; need a bounce above the 50d (~262) to get interested.
Price is near both the 50d and 200d means with positive 12w relative strength vs SPY (+6.5%), but the 4w selloff of -6.6% and RSI 38.6 keep me sidelined until the short-term trend stabilizes.
4w return of +4.0% and strong 4w relative strength (+6.8%) hint at a possible base, but -18.2% drawdown and sub-200d positioning mean the burden of proof is on the bulls; watching 225 as a trigger.

memos.headline: S10 and S04 Show Exceptional Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Flash Red on Margin Compression
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe between durable, high-margin compounders and names where earnings power is deteriorating. S10 stands out with 63.1% net margins, 73.2% YoY revenue growth, and 94.5% net income growth on minimal debt ($8.47B), making it the cleanest fundamental story in the group. S04 is similarly compelling at 47.3% net margins with net income up 59.5% YoY, though its $40.26B debt load warrants monitoring. On the other end, S02 is alarming: despite 12.3% revenue growth, net income collapsed 99.8% to essentially zero, implying massive cost or impairment issues that need explanation before I can get constructive. S09 is also deteriorating with revenue down 1.3% and net income falling 14.6% on a thin 7.9% margin, while carrying $34.24B in debt. I would change my view on S02 if next quarter shows margin recovery above 5%, and on S09 if revenue inflects positive with stable margins.

views.note: 63.1% net margin, 73% revenue growth, 95% earnings growth, and only $8.47B debt — the best fundamental profile in the universe by a wide margin.
47.3% net margin with 59.5% YoY net income growth demonstrates exceptional operating leverage; debt at $40.26B is manageable relative to $38.46B quarterly earnings.
18% revenue growth, 30.3% net margin, 29.8% earnings growth, and low debt of $14.79B make this a solid compounder with a clean balance sheet.
$143.76B revenue growing 15.7% with 29.3% net margins is solid, though $88.50B in total debt is the highest leverage ratio among the profitable names.
Revenue of $213.39B growing 13.6% is impressive on scale, but 9.9% net margin and only 5.9% earnings growth suggest limited operating leverage; would need margin expansion to get constructive.
28.4% net margin is healthy but earnings declined 7% YoY and $435.21B in total debt (likely a financial) dwarfs the rest of the universe; revenue growth of 7.1% is modest.
19.4% net margin is decent but revenue grew only 1.5% and net income fell 6.7% YoY, suggesting stagnation; $25.58B debt on $22.21B quarterly revenue is manageable but not exciting.
18% revenue growth is encouraging but net income fell 13.9% and 12.5% margin is middling; $36.21B debt on $19.13B revenue is elevated and needs watching.
Revenue declining 1.3% with net income down 14.6% and a thin 7.9% margin on $34.24B debt signals deteriorating earnings power I refuse to pay for.
Net income collapsed 99.8% to near zero on $113.22B revenue despite 12.3% top-line growth — margin has effectively evaporated and $78.39B debt makes this uninvestable until clarity emerges.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 3.75% With Sticky Inflation and a Flattening Curve — Favor Defensive Sectors Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been unchanged at 3.75% for three months, down 75bp over the past year, but CPI is running at +2.4% y/y with a 3-month pace of +0.7% (roughly 2.8% annualized), which limits further easing. Unemployment at 4.40% ticked down 10bp over three months but is up 20bp y/y, suggesting a labor market that is softening gently rather than cracking. The 10y yield at 4.28% has drifted up 9bp over three months while the 10y-2y spread has compressed 16bp to +0.51pp, signaling the market is repricing out near-term cuts and flattening the curve — a headwind for banks' net interest margins and for long-duration growth equities. A regime change toward easing would require either a sharp unemployment jump above 4.6% or a sustained CPI print below 2.0% y/y; neither appears imminent, so I position for an extended pause with mild slowdown risk.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds from a 10y yield grinding higher and no imminent rate cuts; stay neutral until the curve signals easing.
Banks are pressured by a flattening 10y-2y spread (down 16bp in 3m to 0.51pp) compressing NIM, with no catalyst for steepening while the Fed pauses.
Staples benefit from a late-cycle pause regime with sticky 2.4% inflation supporting pricing power and defensive positioning as unemployment drifts higher y/y.
Cyclicals face headwinds from a gently softening labor market (unemployment +20bp y/y) and no fresh monetary stimulus to reignite demand.
Energy is macro-neutral here; the pause regime neither boosts nor crushes demand, and inflation at 2.4% is not signaling overheating.
Defensive quality names should outperform in a pause-with-mild-slowdown regime where the Fed is constrained by sticky inflation from cutting further.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S02 and S04 Deeply Negative, S07 and S01 Positive — Watching for Narrative Shifts
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in event-driven sentiment across the universe this quarter. S02 suffered a brutal -19.6% earnings-day reaction on Jan 27, followed by two director departure filings and a Reg FD disclosure — the volume of filings suggests management is in damage-control mode, and I doubt the negative tone has fully washed out. S04 dropped -10.0% on its Jan 28 earnings print with no subsequent positive catalysts to reverse the narrative. On the constructive side, S07 posted a clean +3.4% earnings reaction and S01 gained +2.6%, both with no subsequent negative filings, suggesting positive tone is intact but not yet crowded. S10 is a concern: a -5.5% earnings reaction on Feb 25 compounded by two director departure filings (Jan 23 and Mar 6) signals organizational instability that the market may not have fully discounted.

views.note: Massive -19.6% earnings drop plus rapid-fire director departures and Reg FD filing signal deeply negative and likely still-deteriorating sentiment.
A -10.0% earnings reaction with no subsequent positive catalysts means negative tone is likely still being digested.
Clean +3.4% earnings pop with no negative follow-on filings; positive tone appears genuine but the print is six weeks old so conviction is moderate.
+2.6% earnings reaction and supportive Reg FD disclosure suggest constructive sentiment, though the data is now nearly two months stale.
-5.5% earnings drop compounded by two director departure filings in quick succession points to organizational instability and lingering negative tone.
-5.6% earnings reaction partially offset by a material definitive agreement on Feb 27; tone may be stabilizing but I lack conviction either way.
Muted +0.5% earnings reaction and a routine shareholder vote filing — no strong sentiment signal in either direction.
Near-flat -0.5% earnings reaction followed by routine filings including a director change; sentiment is unremarkable.
Modest +0.6% earnings reaction and a single director change filing — no clear directional tone shift.
No earnings reaction data available; four filings spanning director changes, other events, and Reg FD are routine and provide no strong sentiment read.

memos.headline: Surging Oil Prices and Elevated VIX Signal Structural Geopolitical Risk Repricing Across the Universe
memos.body: I am seeing a macro backdrop dominated by what looks like a significant geopolitical or energy-security shock: WTI crude has surged 52% in one month to $95.61/bbl and 66% over three months, while the VIX has spiked 73% over three months to 27.29, and HY spreads have widened 25bp in a month. The policy uncertainty index at 363 remains elevated even after a 17% monthly decline, suggesting markets have partially digested a policy event but structural risk persists. The flattening yield curve (10y-2y down 16bp over three months to 0.51pp) is consistent with a growth scare layered on top of energy-driven inflation, which constrains the Fed's room to ease. I have moderate-to-high conviction that energy-exposed and supply-chain-concentrated names face headwinds, while any company with pricing power or domestic energy exposure could benefit; a reversal in oil above $100 or new sanctions/export-control announcements would further widen the risk premium. My views below reflect the limited granularity of the 8-K filings available—without explicit detail on each company's geopolitical exposure, I lean on the macro signals and filing frequency as proxies for event sensitivity.

views.note: No 8-K filings in the evidence window and no direct geopolitical signal; staying neutral until more information surfaces.
Three 8-K filings in two months (Jan-Feb) suggest elevated corporate event activity during a period of surging oil and policy uncertainty, raising the risk of adverse geopolitical exposure.
Recent March 9 Reg FD filing may reflect proactive investor communication amid the oil/VIX spike; watching for follow-up but no clear directional edge yet.
Late-February 8-K with both Reg FD and Other Events items coincides with the oil surge; could be supply-chain related but insufficient detail to take a directional stance.
Mid-February Other Events filing during the steepest phase of the oil rally raises concern about cost or supply-chain disruption; avoiding until clarity improves.
January Reg FD filing predates the worst of the oil spike; no subsequent filings suggest the company may be less directly affected, but macro headwinds keep me neutral.
If S09 has domestic energy or defense exposure, the current geopolitical environment could be a tailwind; January filing and absence of distress signals support a cautious long.
Single January Reg FD filing with no follow-up; insufficient geopolitical signal to differentiate from the broad risk-off backdrop.

plan.strategy_name: Selective Quality in a Risk-Off Tape
plan.summary: The universe is deeply bifurcated with elevated VIX, surging oil, and a Fed on pause. I concentrate in the few names where multiple analysts agree on quality or momentum (S05, S09, S10) while keeping a large cash buffer (~45%) given macro headwinds and broad technical weakness.

plans.rationale: Three analysts are constructive: Technical sees a strong 26w uptrend with cushion above the 200d mean, Fundamentals highlights 30% net margins and 30% earnings growth on low debt, and Macro favors defensive names with pricing power in a late-cycle pause. Sentiment is neutral (flat earnings reaction) which is acceptable. The 1w return is positive, suggesting relative resilience.
plans.changes_my_mind: A weekly close below 256 (approximate 200-day mean area cited by Technical) would invalidate the uptrend thesis and trigger an exit.

plans.rationale: Technical is strongly bullish with S09 at 52-week highs, +32.6% over 12 weeks, and RSI not yet overbought. Geopolitics analyst sees a potential energy/defense tailwind from the oil surge. However, Fundamentals flags declining revenue and thin margins, creating a meaningful conflict that sizes this position down. Riding momentum but with a tighter leash.
plans.changes_my_mind: A close below the 50-day mean (~141 implied by Technical) or any earnings pre-announcement showing further margin deterioration would trigger an exit.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals analyst gives the highest conviction long in the universe (63% net margins, 73% revenue growth, 95% earnings growth). However, Sentiment flags a -5.5% earnings reaction and two director departures, and Technical is neutral with price near the 200d mean. The fundamental quality is too strong to ignore entirely, but I size down meaningfully due to the sentiment and organizational instability concerns.
plans.changes_my_mind: A third director departure filing or a close below 165 (roughly 8% below current, breaching recent support) would trigger an exit.

plans.rationale: Sentiment analyst notes a clean +2.6% earnings reaction with supportive Reg FD disclosure. Technical sees positive 12w relative strength vs SPY but the 4w selloff and low RSI keep conviction limited. Fundamentals and Macro are neutral. A small starter position given the sentiment tailwind, but sized very small due to conflicting signals.
plans.changes_my_mind: A close below 143 (roughly 5% stop, near recent support) or any negative 8-K filing would trigger an exit.

plans.rationale: Sentiment is constructive with a clean +3.4% earnings pop and no negative follow-on filings. The massive 26w gain (+64%) shows underlying strength, but Technical warns of volatile consolidation and wants RSI above 50 first. Fundamentals notes declining net income. A tiny position to capture any sentiment-driven bounce, but heavily sized down given the conflicts.
plans.changes_my_mind: RSI failing to reclaim 50 within two weeks or a close below 650 would trigger an exit.
